name: NY-11
label: Likely R

key_factors: Malliotakis has a 40-to-1 fundraising advantage with $2.8M on hand
District leans Republican by about 10 points on PVI

model.rationale: The fundamentals favor the incumbent: a district that leaned Republican by double digits in recent cycles, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger with minimal resources. Markets and the baseline both point to a comfortable Republican win, with only a modest Democratic environment providing any offset.
model.watch: Any late surge in Democratic spending or polling showing DeCillis within single digits would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Nicole Malliotakis seeks a third term in a Staten Island–based district that has leaned Republican in recent cycles. She enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised $2.75 million and holding $2.77 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Michael DeCillis has raised about $68,000. No independent polls of the race are available, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets give the Republican roughly a 93 percent chance of winning. The Democratic candidate faces an uphill climb in a district where the partisan lean favors the GOP by about ten points, though a favorable national environment could narrow the margin somewhat. The race is best characterized as likely Republican, with an upset possible but not expected.
